# Problem 1

```{r load_noaa}
data("ny_noaa")

head(ny_noaa)
dim(ny_noaa)
str(ny_noaa)
```

```{r clean_noaa}
noaa_clean = ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day = day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )

head(noaa_clean)
```

```{r missing_values}
noaa_clean |>
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ sum(is.na(.x))
    )
  )
```

```{r snowfall}
noaa_clean |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```
### NOAA Data Description

The NOAA dataset contains 2,595,176 observations and 7 original variables, including station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, and maximum and minimum temperatures.

The data were cleaned by separating the date into year, month, and day, converting temperatures to degrees Celsius, and converting precipitation to millimeters.

Missing data are common, especially for maximum and minimum temperatures, each with over 1.13 million missing observations.

The most common snowfall value is 0 mm (2,008,508 observations), followed by missing values (381,221). This is expected because most days have no snowfall, and some weather stations do not report snowfall measurements.

```{r january_july_temp}
jan_jul_temp = noaa_clean |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(mean_tmax)) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  jan_jul_temp,
  aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in NY",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
January temperatures are much lower and more variable than July temperatures. January averages range mostly from -10°C to 10°C, while July averages are generally between 20°C and 33°C. There are some unusually low values in both months, but no clear long-term warming or cooling trend is visible from this plot.


```{r temp_snow_plots} 
# Temperature relationship
temp_plot = noaa_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(tmax), !is.na(tmin)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs. Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Snowfall distribution by year
snow_plot = noaa_clean |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, group = year)) +
  geom_density(aes(color = factor(year)), alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Density",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

temp_plot
snow_plot
```


```{r combined_plots}
library(patchwork)

snow_plot = snow_plot +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

combined_plot = temp_plot + snow_plot +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2)

combined_plot
```
Maximum and minimum temperatures show a strong positive relationship, as warmer days generally have higher minimum temperatures.
